content:
{'id': '0', 'text': 'Wen Jiabao, Jia Qinglin and others attend the ceremony'}

{'id': '1', 'text': 'A grand ceremony marking the 100th anniversary of the birth of Jiang Zemin was held at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on Monday (the 17th). General Secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC), President and Chairman of the Central Military Commission Xi Jinping, together with all current Politburo Standing Committee members, were in attendance. Retired leaders including Wen Jiabao, Jia Qinglin, Zhang Dejiang, Yu Zhengsheng, Li Zhanshu, Wang Yang, Li Lanqing, Zeng Qinghong, Li Changchun, He Guoqiang, Liu Yunshan, Wang Qishan and Zhang Gaoli were also present at the ceremony.'}

{'id': '2', 'text': 'Hu Jintao absent; Li Ruihuan, Wu Guanzheng and Luo Gan miss the event'}

{'id': '3', 'text': "However, Hu Jintao, who succeeded Jiang Zemin as CPC General Secretary, President and Chairman of the Central Military Commission, was nowhere to be seen in the live CCTV broadcast. In addition, Li Ruihuan, Wu Guanzheng and Luo Gan — former Politburo Standing Committee members during the Jiang Zemin era — were also absent from today's ceremony."}

{'id': '4', 'text': '"1989 serious political disturbance: Jiang resolutely implemented the Party Central Committee\'s decisions"'}

{'id': '5', 'text': 'In an important address at the ceremony, Xi Jinping reviewed how Jiang Zemin rose from Shanghai Party Secretary to become the core of the third-generation central collective leadership of the CPC. He made particular mention of the fact that: "In the spring and summer of 1989, our country experienced a serious political disturbance. Comrade Jiang Zemin resolutely upheld and implemented the correct decisions of the Party Central Committee, and effectively safeguarded stability in Shanghai."'}

{'id': '6', 'text': 'Xi Jinping also said there is a need to learn from Jiang Zemin\'s "unyielding political faith", describing how, when confronted with the major tests of international turmoil and a serious domestic political disturbance in the late 1980s and early 1990s, Jiang remained unwavering in his commitment to economic construction. He also stressed that governing the country must begin with governing the Party, and that governing the Party must be carried out with strictness.'}

{'id': '7', 'text': 'Xi Jinping also said there is a need to learn from Jiang Zemin\'s "forward-looking strategic thinking", noting that during his tenure Jiang led the smooth return of Hong Kong and Macau, and promoted the reaching of the "1992 Consensus" between the two sides of the Taiwan Strait, which embodies the one-China principle.'}

{'id': '8', 'text': "Outside observers are watching for the political signals sent by Beijing's decision to hold a large-scale commemoration of Jiang Zemin's centenary at this moment, as well as by Xi's speech."}

{'id': '9', 'text': "Independent political scholar Chen Daoyin said that holding large-scale commemorative events on the centenary of a deceased leader is a longstanding institutional practice. Many important leaders in the past, including Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping, have had grand centenary commemorations held in their honour. As the core of the CPC's third-generation central collective leadership, it is entirely in keeping with established practice and protocol for Jiang Zemin to have a large-scale centenary commemoration."}

{'id': '10', 'text': 'Scholar: Remarks on 1989 contain no new formulations'}

{'id': '11', 'text': 'Regarding Xi\'s active mention of Jiang Zemin\'s political stance in 1989 during the commemoration, Chen Daoyin said 1989 was a crucial turning point for both Chinese politics and Jiang Zemin\'s political career. That year, Jiang "chose the right side", and — having been a local leader on the verge of retirement — was entrusted with a critical mission, transferred to Beijing to replace Zhao Ziyang, and became the core of the CPC\'s third-generation central collective leadership. Hence, reviewing his life necessarily requires mentioning the events of 1989.'}

{'id': '12', 'text': 'Chen Daoyin noted that Jiang\'s resolute defence of the Party Central Committee\'s decisions at the time echoes the political requirement of "two upholds" that Xi currently emphasises, making it all the more necessary to raise the matter again. He also believes Xi\'s remarks on 1989 are essentially "definitive" formulations, containing no new expressions. There is no need for outside observers to over-interpret Xi\'s renewed mention of 1989, he added.'}

{'id': '13', 'text': "As for the large-scale commemoration of Jiang Zemin's centenary, Hu Jintao — the core of the CPC's fourth-generation central collective leadership — was absent. Chen Daoyin said that, although retired leaders are not necessarily obliged to attend such events, logically Hu, as Jiang's direct successor, would be expected to show up at a major commemoration of his predecessor. His absence could be because he was not in Beijing, or due to health reasons. He pointed out that attention should be paid to whether Hu Jintao sends a wreath to the funeral of Zhu Rongji on Tuesday (the 18th)."}

{'id': '14', 'text': 'Zhao Jianmin, former dean of the College of Social Sciences at Chinese Culture University in Taiwan, who specialises in Chinese political development and cross-strait relations, believes Xi\'s speech today constitutes a comprehensive review of Jiang Zemin\'s life. Several pivotal moments in Jiang\'s political career — including the introduction of the important thought of "Three Represents", the reaching of the "1992 Consensus" across the Taiwan Strait, and his resolute support for the Party Central Committee\'s decisions in 1989 — are all subjects that cannot be avoided when reviewing Jiang\'s legacy.'}

{'id': '15', 'text': "Zhao Jianmin said that Xi only touched upon Jiang's firm stance on the side of the Party Central Committee in 1989, without making any further remarks on the June 4th incident, and that this is a normal way of handling the matter."}

{'id': '16', 'text': 'Zhao Jianmin also pointed out that Xi\'s emphasis on Jiang Zemin\'s centenary has personal factors. He believes Xi\'s subsequent promotion — being transferred from a leadership post in Fujian to serve as the "top leader" of major economic provinces Zhejiang and Shanghai — laid the foundation for his eventual rise to the top leadership, and that Jiang Zemin played an important and crucial role in that process.'}

{'id': '17', 'text': "He believes Xi's emphasis on commemorative activities for Jiang Zemin demonstrates, on the one hand, Xi's sense of gratitude and old affection; on the other hand, by evaluating Jiang, Xi is emphasising Jiang's promotion of strict Party governance and anti-corruption work, thereby showing that related policies are a continuation and inheritance of the direction set during the Jiang era. This is the implementation of an existing consensus within the Party, and serves to clarify rumours circulating in society."}

{'id': '18', 'text': 'Highlight the importance of obeying the Party Central Committee at moments of major right and wrong'}

{'id': '19', 'text': 'However, veteran Chinese political commentator Cai Shenkun holds a different view. He described it as rare for Xi to publicly mention Jiang Zemin\'s stance during the 1989 "political disturbance", noting that during Jiang\'s lifetime, and even after his death, his family hoped to play down rather than emphasise how Jiang rose to the centre of supreme power as a result of the June 4th incident.'}

{'id': '20', 'text': "Cai Shenkun believes that Xi's deliberate raising of this point on this occasion is intended to highlight the importance of obeying the Party Central Committee and maintaining political loyalty at moments of major right and wrong."}

{'id': '21', 'text': 'In addition, Cai Shenkun noted that the 21st National Congress of the Communist Party of China (abbreviated as the "Party\'s 21st Congress") is expected to be held next autumn. He believes that Xi\'s emphasis on Jiang Zemin\'s centenary and his praise of Jiang\'s resolute choice to stand with the Party Central Committee serves a dual purpose: on one hand, it emphasises the political lineage between Xi and Jiang, reinforcing the legitimacy of political continuity; on the other hand, by commemorating Jiang, it reiterates to Party members the importance of obeying the Central Committee and maintaining political loyalty.'}
